hard_limits.note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every threshold the validator enforces, read live from autonomy_config.json this run. Any number quoted in CLAUDE.md prose is DESCRIPTIVE — when the two disagree, these values win, because these are the ones the code actually checks. (CLAUDE.md stated RR >= 1.0 for two days after the floor was raised to 2.0 on 2026-07-16, so every proposal built against the prose was rejected on arrival.)

position_sizing._notional_cap_note: Notional ceilings only. Risk-based sizing below is the binding constraint: a tight-stop setup may size up to these ceilings for the same 1% risk; a wide-stop setup sizes well under them. Raised from 10%/$1000 when risk-based sizing landed (2026-07-16). Rebased 10x DOWN on 2026-07-21 when the book was restated from a $10,000 start to a $1,000 start: every percentage stays identical, only the notional ceilings moved ($2000 -> $200, conviction $3000 -> $300, min clamp $200 -> $20). See _fractional_stop_note below — the smaller book changes what the broker can protect.

risk_based_sizing._note: Van Tharp / Elder / Turtle framework (research 2026-07-16, user-approved). Every BUY risks at most risk_per_trade_pct of equity measured entry-to-stop; the validator CLAMPS oversized proposals down to the risk budget rather than rejecting. Portfolio heat = sum over open positions of entry-basis committed risk max(0,(avg_cost-stop)*qty)/equity; new BUYs are rejected past portfolio_heat_cap_pct (user chose 8%; literature 6-10%). Theme cap: committed initial risk sharing one demand_driver <= theme_initial_risk_cap_pct. Entry-basis heat means trailed stops above cost free the budget (pyramiding into winners stays possible). momentum_unwind_risk_scale halves the risk budget when momentum_health flags an unwind.

scale_in._note: Adds allowed only into winners (price above blended cost, never averaging down), max 2 adds, combined exposure stays inside the per-name cap. Partial exits via sell_fraction in (0,1].

conviction_tier._note: When earned, conviction raises the RISK budget to 1.5% (and the notional ceilings accordingly); base tier stays 1%.

position_sizing._fractional_stop_note: CONSEQUENCE OF THE $1,000 BOOK, measured 2026-07-21 against the live 187-name universe. Alpaca carries fractional quantities only with time_in_force=day, so a GTC stop needs a whole-share leg (execution/alpaca_broker.py, MIN_WHOLE_SHARES_FOR_LIMIT=4 and _resting stop arming). At a $1,429 position (the $10,000 book) 69.5% of the universe got a full exchange-held GTC stop attached at entry and only 2.1% fell under one share. At a $143 position (this book) those become 3.2% and 72.2%: most entries are now sub-one-share, so their protective stop is a DAY order that expires at the close and is re-armed by scripts/stop_watch.py on the Actions cron. Intraday protection is a real resting broker order and is essentially unchanged; what is lost is the overnight/weekend leg, where the exit now depends on the poller's next tick rather than the opening print. Accepted deliberately: the gap risk is real but denominated in single-digit dollars at this size. Do NOT read a low whole-share count as a reason to skip a setup.

quality._variant_perception_note: Every BUY must state the market's misunderstanding explicitly: what consensus believes, what the agent believes differently, the specific mispriced mechanism, and the event/date when the market finds out. Enforced as a required BUY field; format documented in CLAUDE.md.
quality._risk_map_scenarios_note: risk_map and scenarios were always in the CLAUDE.md schema but not validator-enforced, so proposals omitted scenarios and the published scenario_ev stayed empty. Now required on every BUY.
quality._thesis_invalidators_note: Binding falsifiers (not vibes): object with invalidating_print, invalidating_structure, time_box — each a non-empty string. Enforced on every BUY so re-underwrites have kill criteria.
quality._demand_driver_note: Primary demand-driver theme for theme concentration (e.g. hyperscaler_server_capex, ai_compute_gpu). Distinct from GICS sector. See tools/demand_drivers.py and context bundle demand_driver_map.
quality._required_sell_fields_note: SELL_TO_CLOSE needs only these; the BUY-oriented required_proposal_fields list used to reject legitimate discretionary exits for missing stop_loss/target_price. Prefer also exit_reason when available (process, not hard-required).
quality._claim_grounding_note: Added 2026-07-25, DEFAULT OFF pending evidence, same staged rollout as _tradeability_note below. WHAT IT DOES: validator._check_claim_grounding greps every entity a BUY's variant_perception/catalysts name against the FULL context bundle and rejects the ones that appear nowhere in it. Built from four real incidents the LLM risk desk caught by hand: DDOG 07-22 ('JMP Securities raised its target to $311' - the string 'JMP' appears ZERO times in that day's bundle), MELI 07-24 ('Loggi acquisition', a Citi fair-value cut, '14 new Brazil fulfillment centers'), IBKR 07-22 (an invented 'fourth consecutive beat' with an EMPTY guidance_ledger), UNP 07-24 (a 'binding MOU signed one day earlier' that inverts the actual sequence). WHY IT IS NOT ON YET: CLAUDE.md step 5 makes WebSearch MANDATORY before any BUY, so the brain is REQUIRED to bring in facts that legitimately are not in the bundle - blocking on 'absent from bundle' would reject true WebSearch findings alongside fabricated ones, and a false rejection costs a real trade on a book that has already gone days without one. Until proposals carry per-claim sources, the SAME computation is fed to the risk desk every run (validator.unsourced_claims -> runlib.brain_io), which can weigh the WebSearch context a regex cannot. TO ENABLE: watch the risk-desk prompt's UNSOURCED CLAIMS block for a week; if the entities it lists are consistently real fabrications rather than WebSearch-sourced truth, flip this to true. Precision was tuned against the 7 real BUY proposals in journal/proposals + journal/rejected: multi-word candidates are only taken from an explicit attribution pattern ('<Firm> raised/said/cut'), because the bare proper-noun pass produced prose fragments like 'MINIMUM CONTRACTED' and 'Case After Strong' that no bundle would ever contain verbatim.

calibration_probe._note: ADDED 2026-08-05. A BUY scored honestly in [0.50, 0.60) is no longer rejected outright: it trades as a CALIBRATION PROBE at risk_scale x the normal risk budget (0.5% of equity instead of 1%), stamped calibration_probe on the proposal AND persisted onto the position's plan at fill, with at most max_open_probes such positions on the book at once (validator._check_probe_limits). WHY: the hard 0.60 floor could never learn whether 0.50-0.60 setups win, because it never let one trade - HPE on 2026-08-05 died at 0.57 the same afternoon a validated DXCM entry died on a keyword false-positive, on a book that had made 3 trades in a month - and its only lasting lesson to the proposer was that honesty costs the trade while writing 0.62 sails through. The desk's confidence haircut (max -0.10) previously turned into a death sentence whenever it landed under 0.60; now it converts the trade to half-risk instead, so the desk can express skepticism without killing the setup. Probe fills grade into their own 0.50-0.60 bucket (tools/performance_breakdown._confidence_bucket), so once 5+ close the existing calibration machinery has REAL fill data: if the bucket proves losing (<40% WR) the losing-bucket gate starts rejecting it with evidence, and if it proves fine that argues the floor down. Every other gate - RR>=2, geometry, volatility stop, heat, theme caps, earnings window, risk desk - applies to a probe at full strength; below probe min_confidence remains a hard rejection.

earnings_window._note: ADDED 2026-08-03. Until now there was NO coded earnings rule anywhere - `days_to_earnings` appeared ZERO times in validator.py - so 'trade around the binary' was entirely the brain's judgment applied against a 45-day default horizon. In earnings season that excludes essentially the whole universe, and it did: across 2026-07-13..08-03 run after run passed on every candidate for a print somewhere inside the swing window (08-03 alone rejected MPC and AMGN for an 08-04 print, then NET and TEAM for 08-06, and traded nothing). The gate is now NARROW and the narrowness is the point: only a print within pre_print_blackout_days blocks a BUY, everything outside it is explicitly tradeable, and a name that has ALREADY reported within post_print_drift_days is a PREFERRED lane (the binary is resolved and the geometry is clean). allow_trade_through_with_case lets the brain trade the print deliberately when the binary IS the thesis, by supplying an `earnings_case` of >= min_earnings_case_chars. Fail-open: a ticker the committed calendar does not carry is NOT MEASURED, never 'no print'.

quality._min_rr_note: Raised 1.0 -> 2.0 (2026-07-16, user-approved after expectancy research): breakeven win rate at 2:1 is 33%, keeping the book profitable across the realistic 40-55% band; a 1:1 floor loses money below ~52% wins after costs (Minervini/O'Neil both demand ~2:1 at entry).
quality._volatility_stop_note: A stop tighter than the name's noise is not protection - it exits on ordinary volatility, not on a broken thesis. The stop must sit at least max(min_stop_atr_multiple x 14d-ATR%, min_stop_expected_move_fraction x options expected_move%) below entry. Enforced only when volatility data is present (fail-open). If that floor exceeds max_stop_loss_distance_pct, the name is too volatile for a valid swing stop and is rejected.
quality._trailing_stop_note: Chandelier exit (LeBeau/Elder; user-approved 2026-07-16): once a position's high-water mark puts (high_water - 3xATR) ABOVE the plan stop, the effective stop ratchets up with it - never down, never widened, and deliberately NO breakeven jump at +1R (research shows early breakeven moves gut trend expectancy). Forced exits fire on the effective stop; reason trailing_stop_breached when the trail was binding.
quality._falsifiability_note: ADDED 2026-07-19 (audit). variant_perception, scenarios and thesis_invalidators were PRESENCE-checked only, while CLAUDE.md twice called variant_perception 'validator-enforced' - a single non-space character satisfied it. min_invalidator_chars was 12, so 'drops below 50dma' (17) passed as a binding falsifier. scenarios' probabilities need not have summed to 1, and tools/scenario_ev.py computed honest EV whose only callers were two RENDERING paths. Now: invalidating_print needs a numeric threshold, time_box needs a date or day-count, variant_perception needs a figure and a dated resolution, and scenario probabilities must sum to ~1 with a non-negative probability-weighted return. These check SHAPE, not argument quality - no regex grades a thesis, and the risk desk and the reader remain the judges of that.

theme_risk._note: Market value of positions sharing the same demand_driver plus proposed size must stay under this fraction of equity. Catches DELL+HPE style single-factor books that sector caps miss when names sit in different GICS sleeves. Fail-open if demand_driver missing (field check already rejects). The notional cap here complements the RISK-based theme cap in position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.theme_initial_risk_cap_pct.

regime_gate._note: Coded regime filter (Faber 2007/2013: ~halved max drawdown over a century; user-approved 2026-07-16). When the benchmark trend is hostile (SPY below its 200DMA), new BUYs are REJECTED (regime_gate_spy_below_200dma) - exits and holds are never blocked, and existing stops keep working, consistent with the evidence that the filter's value is blocking NEW risk, not forced liquidation. Momentum-unwind detection (tools/momentum_health.py) separately halves the risk budget via position_sizing.risk_based_sizing.momentum_unwind_risk_scale rather than hard-blocking. Fail-open when regime data is absent from market_context.

book_risk._unknown_beta_note: ADDED 2026-08-03. The beta ceiling used to reject outright whenever ANY name in the projected book lacked a beta in the correlation feed, and on 2026-07-28 that killed a BKR BUY whose only unknown name was BKR itself against a 100%-CASH book - a $49 position on a $984 book cannot make anything a leveraged index bet, and the same trade was re-proposed and filled hours later. Failing closed on an unmeasurable input is right when the input could hide real exposure; it is wrong when the worst case is computable. Unknown betas on the PROPOSED name are now assumed to be this value (deliberately pessimistic - the ceiling itself) and the cap is enforced against that. HELD positions missing a beta still fail closed: an exposure already carried cannot be bounded by sizing, and only the one being added can.
book_risk._tradeability_note: Added 2026-07-19, both DEFAULT OFF pending evidence. Both floors currently fail OPEN on missing data: a proposal on a ticker absent from market_context skips the stop noise-band check entirely (a 1% stop on an 8%-ATR name passes), and a name with no market-cap figure clears the $1B floor by default. The enforcement is built and tested; enabling is a one-line flip once the evidence is in. require_volatility_data: a live gather covers 182/187 tickers with ZERO universe names absent, so the coverage case is already strong - held off only because 26 existing tests pass market_context={} and rewriting that many safety fixtures hours before going live is how a real assertion gets weakened by accident. Enable after a week of runs, then fix the fixtures deliberately. require_market_cap_data: weaker case and it stays off longer. market_cap_usd is NOT a bundle field (0% coverage there); orchestrator.py resolves it PER PROPOSAL from deep_fundamentals, then scan rows, then a LIVE lookup - so a yfinance hiccup would block every BUY in the run. Blocking the whole book on a network blip is a worse failure than the fail-open it replaces, and the weekly universe review already bars sub-$1B names from entering. Enable only once per-proposal resolution is observed at ~100%.
book_risk._note: Book-level risk (added 2026-07-19 after an audit found every binding constraint was arithmetic on ONE proposal while portfolio_beta / shared_left_tail / corr_to_book were computed by tools/correlation.py and consumed only as prose). Four controls, all in tools/book_risk.py, all pure. (1) max_factor_stack_pct: aggregate notional across factor_map.AI_STACK_DRIVERS. The 2% per-driver risk cap permits ~2 positions per driver, so 8 positions across 4 AI-stack drivers was 100% AI exposure passing every existing limit - a per-driver cap is not a factor cap. (2) gap_adjusted_heat: the 8% heat cap sums (cost-stop)*qty, which assumes stops FILL AT THE STOP - contradicted by execution_costs.stop_gap_atr_fraction (0.5) in this same file, and by the only closed stop in the ledger (DELL plan stop 408.00, fill 389.75, 4.5% through, realized -13.5% on a position sized for 1%). Heat now adds the modelled gap-through, using correlation only to decide how much of the book gaps on the same morning - NEVER to hand budget back, since the plain sum is already the fully-correlated case. Unknown correlation assumes the worst. (3) max_portfolio_beta: MV-weighted against EQUITY not invested capital, so a half-cash book reads as half-exposed. (4) stress_scenarios: named shocks priced against the book the proposal WOULD create; losses deliberately NOT floored at stops, because a shock worth naming is one where stops gap. driver_shocks key __ai_stack__ shocks the whole factor group. All four fail CLOSED on unverifiable inputs, matching the portfolio_heat_unverifiable precedent.

learning_controls._note: Code-enforced Learning Protocol. Under min_trades_for_binding: no hard rejections from calibration_gate. At/above: high-conf inflation caps confidence; losing sector/theme buckets require calibration_exception text. Shadow book binds caution at 8 closed shadows (separate).
learning_controls._target_calibration_note: Added 2026-07-19. min_risk_reward_ratio (2.0) is the system's most rigorously justified rule - the config carries the expectancy math - and it is computed from the LLM's own target_price, which appears ZERO times in execution/exit_guard.py. Exits are stop, trail or horizon only; CLAUDE.md calls the target 'a milestone, not a tripwire'. So the gate filtered on a number nothing enforced or graded, and the model could always clear it by writing a bigger one. Targets stay NON-BINDING for exits (letting winners run is correct and literature-supported) - instead every close is graded on claimed RR vs REALIZED RR and target attainment. Binds only at min_trades_for_binding closed trades; at n=2 it reports phase 'anecdote' and withholds the binding-grade number entirely.

engagement.note: TRIGGER ACCOUNTABILITY: every name in watchlist_trigger_alerts that you do not BUY this run owes a `trigger_reviews` row — action buy | drop | requalify, a reason >=25 chars, and for requalify a NEW level. stop_engineering.note: ENFORCED stop floor per name. Your stop_loss must sit at least min_stop_distance_pct below entry or the validator rejects it (stop_inside_noise_band). This is a floor, not a target - for a swing hold, aim WIDER (roughly 1.5-2x ATR, or clearly beyond the expected move) so ordinary volatility does not stop you out. If tradeable is false the name is too volatile for a valid stop under the 15% cap; do not propose it.

position_stop_cushion.note: For each open position: room left between today's price and your recorded stop, measured in the name's own ATR. cushion_in_atr < 1 (inside_noise_band true) means one ordinary session could hit the stop - decide deliberately (hold through it, or exit on your terms) rather than get noise-stopped. The safety layer still enforces the recorded stop on a closing basis.

process_checklist.note: Required reasoning order every run. Work top-down; do not propose a BUY before completing the steps above it. Cite the relevant context-bundle blocks in commentary when a step changes your aggression.

steps.title: Macro regime check
steps.must: Read macro_regime (+ market_events / market_news tape). State whether the regime supports adding long swing exposure. Hostile or rolling leadership -> raise the bar, prefer cash / exits.

steps.title: Portfolio / book review
steps.must: Re-underwrite every open position with fresh research: HOLD or SELL_TO_CLOSE. Thesis broken = exit. Cash test: if remaining expected return no longer clearly beats cash yield, rotate. Honor stops, stall flags, and forced-exit aftermath.

steps.title: Idea selection
steps.must: From universe_scan / watchlist / tape promotions, pick at most a handful of candidates. Prefer fat pitches over marginal RR. Empty proposals with a clear no_trade_reason is a valid outcome.

steps.title: Entry geometry & underwrite
steps.must: For each candidate: charts, volume, stop/target geometry, fundamentals freshness, filings, catalysts. WebSearch mandatory before proposing a BUY. Variant perception required. Size and RR must clear validator floors as a MINIMUM, not a target.

steps.title: Kill conditions
steps.must: State what kills the trade and how you would know early (risk_map). Pre-plan stop, horizon, and invalidation before size. If kill conditions are fuzzy, do not buy — watchlist it.

reasoning_process.full_run_no_trade_rule: On full depth with empty proposals, include rejected_ideas: [{ticker, reason}, ...] with at least 2 scan ideas you passed on.

price_freshness.note: Prefer universe_scan.prices_meta[T].price_as_of (bar session date) over bundle age alone. On catalyst days, verify live before chasing a trigger on a lagging close.

watchlist_feedback.note: Watchlist foresight / opportunity-cost feedback. hits_not_bought = names still on the watchlist whose stated buy level was reached but you never bought. opportunity_cost = large moves (or hit-then-dropped) without action — grade whether the pass was discipline or a miss. recent.topic: Fibonacci 38.2–61.8% is a pullback ALERT ZONE that only earns a would_buy_at when it co-locates with a named rail (20-day / 50-DMA / last swing) — standalone Fib levels are not a bounce edge
recent.summary: ChartSchool frames Fibonacci retracements as ALERT ZONES, not hard reversal points: after a swing advance you mark 23.6/38.2/50/61.8% of that leg, watch the 38.2–61.8% band (50% is Dow Theory's half-retracement, not a Fib ratio), and still need candlesticks, volume, oscillators, or moving averages to confirm a turn. Practitioner swing guides agree that the useful case is CONFLUENCE — a Fib band sitting on the same price as a 20/50/200-DMA or prior support — not a lone 61.8% line. The academic record is load-bearing and I keep it. Batchelor and Ramyar (Cass, 2006) find Dow price/time ratios around Fib and round fractions occur no more often than a stationary block bootstrap expects — magic-number clustering can be dismissed. Tsinaslanidis et al. (Expert Systems with Applications, 2022) similarly find bounce probabilities on Fib zones statistically indistinguishable from random non-Fib S&R zones, and Fib trading rules do not beat the random-zone benchmark or buy-and-hold. So the ratios are not a measured edge; they are a shared-attention map that sometimes coincides with real structure. Sources disagree on whether self-fulfilling anchoring rescues standalone Fib (practitioner yes; rigorous tests no) — the honest resolution for this book is: never promote a Fib touch alone; only use the band when it names the same invalidation geometry as the rails and swing lows we already trust.
recent.how_to_apply: On a Stage-2 pullback candidate (above_200dma, trend_up_50_over_200, rel_strength_3m_pct still constructive), identify the last confirmed thrust swing low→high and note where 38.2–61.8% of that leg sits. Promote to would_buy_at ONLY when that band co-locates (± roughly one ATR or a tight price cluster) with a named rail this book already uses — rising 20-day (KB-3099641994), 50-DMA (KB-4252672139), or the last confirmed higher low (KB-2454897375) — AND volume is drying (no_supply / KB-2413484258 / KB-6241168493). Write the trigger as the rail hold or light-volume reclaim, not 'Fib 61.8 bounce'. Place stop_loss beyond the deeper of the Fib-band failure and the last confirmed swing low, floored by stop_engineering.min_stop_distance_pct / ATR rules, and require ≥2:1 to the first overhead supply or measured target (KB-6231300499). Never loosen the fat-pitch bar or size up because price 'hit golden Fib'. If Fib and the rails disagree, trust the rail and the swing invalidation — Fib alone is not evidence.

recent.topic: ATR-stop 1% sizing is not a gap-risk bound: when a binary print sits inside the hold window, size against the options expected move (or exit/skip) — the stop cannot fire overnight
recent.summary: Practitioner and options literature agree on a structural fact: stop-loss orders only work while the exchange is open. An after-close or pre-open earnings print reprices in one overnight gap, so a stop at entry−1.5×ATR fills at the open — often well past the intended level (Longbridge; Traders Agency). That breaks the usual share-count formula shares = (equity×1%) / stop_distance: the PLANNED 1R is a day-session intent, not a hard overnight loss bound. Pomegra’s earnings sizing chapter makes the same point from the Kelly/fractional side — standard fixed-fractional sizing is dangerously optimistic when gap risk can 2–3× the planned R, so professionals cut the risk fraction (often to ~0.25–0.75%) or size against the maximum adverse gap, not the stop. The market already publishes that gap scale as the ATM straddle expected move; this book’s options_signals.expected_move_pct and the validator’s min_stop_expected_move_fraction=0.5 already treat EM as a noise floor for STOP PLACEMENT. The missing half is SIZE: when days_to_earnings falls inside holding_horizon_days (outside the coded 3-day blackout, or inside it with an earnings_case), the honest 1% budget is shares × price × EM% ≤ ~1% equity — or half-size / exit-before-print / wait for the post-print drift lane. Sources agree the tools are sizing and the pre-decision to step aside, not a tighter ATR stop. Sources disagree on the exact haircut (half-size vs EM-dollar bound vs skip); the common principle is that planned-R from an A
recent.how_to_apply: Before any BUY (and on every holdings review of an open name), read days_to_earnings / earnings_week and options_signals.expected_move_pct. If the print falls inside holding_horizon_days: (1) prefer the existing pre-print fork — exit into strength before the print, or wait for the post_print_drift lane — rather than hope the ATR stop saves you; (2) if you still hold or deliberately trade through (earnings_case ≥80 chars inside the 3-day blackout), recompute size so shares × mark × EM% ≤ the 1% risk budget (use half-size when EM is noisy/missing), and write that EM-dollar max loss into the plan; (3) never ‘fix’ overnight binary risk by tightening stop_loss inside the ATR / 0.5×EM floor — that only worsens day-session noise exits and does nothing to the gap. On the current NOW seat, apply the same re-underwrite when its next print enters the horizon: cushion-in-ATR is a day-session metric, not a gap bound.

recent.topic: Opening-range breakout is a daytrade construct: do not promote a 5–60 minute ORH print into a 3–90 day swing entry — wait for daily acceptance (or a daily NR compression break) instead
recent.summary: Toby Crabel's Opening Range Breakout (ORB) defines the high and low of the first N minutes of the RTH session (commonly 5, 30, or 60) and trades a break of that opening-range high (ORH) or low (ORL). Practitioner and system literature treat ORB as an INTRADAY framework: institutional order flow and volatility cluster at the open, the edge is session-scoped, and responsible implementations force an end-of-day exit because overnight gap risk was never part of the design (Build Alpha; Pomegra ORB playbook). Academic-style daytrade tests that look impressive (e.g. high relative-volume 'stocks in play' on a 5-minute ORB) are measuring SAME-DAY momentum, not multi-day swing expectancy — extrapolating those stats into a 3–90 day hold is a category error. The only swing-usable cousin from the same Crabel family is daily-bar volatility compression (NR4/NR7: the narrowest daily range of the last 4 or 7 sessions), which StockCharts and Crabel both frame as a contraction-before-expansion FILTER that is directionally neutral and still needs a larger Stage-2 / fat-pitch context; even then, modern cost-aware backtests of standalone NR7 breakouts are often unprofitable (Validated Strategies NR7 on gold 2017–2026: information vs random, but negative expectancy after costs). For this book the practical rule is negative: a morning ORH break on a watchlist name is not an entry trigger, not a 'confirmation' that upgrades an unfinished daily pivot, and not a reason to loosen the fat-pitch bar. recent.how_to_apply: During gather/act, if a candidate's 'trigger' is a 5–60 minute opening-range high break, an IB (initial balance) break, or 'confirmed above the first-hour high', treat that as NOT an entry — decline or leave it on the watchlist until the daily pivot is accepted (close above the named level, or a constructive throwback/reclaim of that daily level on light supply). Do not widen size, shorten the ATR stop, or loosen the fat-pitch bar because the open 'looked confirmed'. NR7 / tight daily compression may SUPPORT an already-valid VCP / 3-weeks-tight / inner-pivot story as evidence the base is coiling, but it never replaces Stage-2 location, 2:1 RR, or the written invalidation under the last confirmed swing low. recent.topic: 1% sizing is deep-fractional Kelly AND the inverse-vol scaler — do not double-cut ATR or apologize for small size
recent.summary: The two sizing questions — how much to risk per trade, and whether a second ATR haircut is needed — are one theory. Kelly f* = W - (1-W)/R maps onto the 1%-of-equity entry-to-stop budget. On realistic swing parameters (2:1 RR, 40–55% wins) full Kelly is ~10–32.5%, so 1% is ~1/10 to 1/30 of full Kelly — deep-fractional BY DESIGN. With a tiny closed-trade sample edge is unmeasured, and MacLean–Thorp–Ziemba show overbetting is asymmetric: a 10% edge overestimate drives ~50% overbet and the growth parabola hits zero at 2× Kelly. Half-Kelly keeps ~75% of growth at half size, so erring LOW is correct. Van Tharp splits percent-risk (P = equity × risk% / stop) from percent-volatility (P = equity × vol% / ATR). They coincide iff the stop is an ATR multiple. This book's size = (equity × 1%) / stop_distance_pct is percent-risk; the ATR/expected-move floor already makes it inverse-vol, so a second discretionary ATR cut double-counts. Equal-dollar notionals silently overweight loud names. Kelly also assumes independent bets: the 8% heat and 2% theme caps ARE the portfolio-Kelly constraint when corr/demand_driver collapses names into one bet. Time-series vol-management (Moreira–Muir ~50% cut) is already coded as the 0.5× unwind haircut plus the hostile gate — do not add a third discretionary vol cut or stand-down.
recent.how_to_apply: On every BUY, place stop_loss beyond the named structural low AND at least stop_engineering.min_stop_distance_pct (aim 1.5–2×ATR, never past 15%), then size = (equity × 1%) / stop_distance_pct — that single fraction is both the 1R budget and the inverse-vol scaler. Do not also cut the 1% because ATR looks high, and do not treat the 1% floor as too small to take a clean setup. Before any BUY run the one-bet test with portfolio_risk and demand_driver_map: co-movers >~0.7 or shared demand_driver share the 2% theme / 8% heat budget. If stop_engineering.tradeable is false (ATR/EM floor exceeds the 15% cap), pass — do not squeeze the stop or inflate the target. Leave the coded 0.5× unwind haircut and hostile regime gate alone; never add a discretionary third vol cut or cash stand-down on top of 1%.

recent.topic: Shadow-regret discipline on skips: grade the written bar at decision time, never loosen it because a rejected idea later printed +10%
recent.summary: This book's shadow portfolio currently surfaces multiple regret_misses (OKTA/PANW/CRWD rejected_idea paths that later reached ~+10%, PLTR watchlist_hold ~+13%). The temptation is to treat that counterfactual upside as proof the fat-pitch bar was too tight and to buy the next similar name. That is resulting applied to NON-trades: judging a skip by the path the stock took after the decision, not by whether the written criteria (Street upside ≥10%, Stage-2 rails, momentum not decelerating, catalyst quality) were unmet at the time. Annie Duke's resulting framework (Thinking in Bets / How to Decide) says a good decision with a bad outcome is still a good decision; the mirror is that a correct skip that later 'would have worked' is still a correct skip when the information set at T0 failed the bar. Practitioner writeups on regret aversion (Capital.com; Enlightened Stock Trading) show the same trap on entries: fear of future FOMO pushes traders to override systems, while systemic pre-commitment is the antidote. Barber & Odean (FAJ 1999; JoF 1998 disposition work) add the portfolio-level warning: individual investors who trade more actively earn lower returns — loosening a curated bar to chase shadow upside is the overtrading channel dressed as learning. Honest nuance: shadow regrets ARE useful as SAMPLE diagnostics. If a cluster of good_skip grades flips to bad_skip because one criterion systematically fails (e.g. Street-mean floor misfires on momentum leaders), revise THAT criterio
recent.how_to_apply: On every brain slot, when seat_reviews or rejected_ideas include a name that later appears in shadow regret_misses (OKTA/PANW/CRWD-class cyber skips, or watchlist_hold like PLTR), do NOT re-open a BUY because max_upside_pct printed after the skip. Re-read the original reject reason against today's tape: only propose if TODAY's print clears the live bar (Street mean ≥10% above mark, Stage-2, momentum not decelerating, catalyst not a board/8-K shuffle). In commentary, label a maintained skip as good_skip when the T0 bar was unmet, even if shadow shows +10%. Escalate a bar change only via study/config — never by sneaking a below-bar BUY to soothe FOMO. Keep the 1% risk / 2:1 RR / ATR-floored stop unchanged; regret does not resize risk.

HOUSTON – September 2, 2026 – HPE (NYSE: HPE) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended July 31, 2026.
“HPE’s strategy is proving itself again this quarter. Our results demonstrate the durability of our profitable growth momentum. We delivered record revenue, orders, and profitability, fueled by surging customer demand across our portfolio,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE. “AI is becoming a multi-year growth driver for HPE, and our differentiated portfolio positions us to capture that opportunity at scale.”
“Our outstanding revenue performance and expanded profitability in the third quarter reflect robust demand across our portfolio and consistent, disciplined execution,” said Marie Myers, executive vice president and CFO of HPE. “With our Q3 results and our order backlog at a record level, we are raising our financial outlook and plan to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4.”
Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Financial Results
•Revenue: $12.2 billion, up 34% from the prior-year period
•Gross margins:
◦GAAP of 40.1%, up 1,090 basis points from the prior-year period and up 360 basis points sequentially

•Operating profit margins:
◦GAAP of 11.4%, up 870 basis points from the prior-year period and up 440 basis points sequentially
◦Non-GAAP(1) of 16.2%, up 770 basis points from the prior-year period and up 290 basis points sequentially
•Diluted net earnings per share (“EPS”):
◦GAAP of $1.06, up $0.85 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.84 - $0.89
◦Non-GAAP(1) of $1.11, up $0.67 from the prior-year period and above our outlook range of $0.88 - $0.93
•Cash flow from operations: $1.6 billion, an increase of $0.3 billion from the prior-year period

▪Campus & Branch was $1.4 billion, up 31.0% from the prior-year period.
▪Data Center Networking was $382 million, up 112.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Security was $281 million, up 75.6% from the prior-year period.
▪Routing was $788 million, up 270.0% from the prior-year period.
•Cloud & AI revenue was $9.0 billion, up 25.4% from the prior-year period, with 17.0% operating profit margin, compared to 7.0% from the prior-year period.
◦Within Cloud & AI, revenue from:
▪Server was $6.8 billion, up 35.3% from the prior-year period.
▪Storage was $1.3 billion, up 10.2% from the prior-year period.
▪Financial Services was $0.9 billion, down 0.3% from the prior-year period.
•Corporate Investments and Other revenue was $278 million, up 3.0% from the prior-year period, with -24.1% of operating profit margin, compared to -7.0% from the prior-year period.

HPE is raising expectations for non-GAAP diluted net EPS growth to be in the range of 16% to 20%(1)(4). HPE estimates non-GAAP operating margin rate to be in the range of 14% to 15%(1)(4). financial_checklists.note: Per-focus-name financial-line checklists by business model. Use the weight line: different models, different scoreboards.

NOW.label: Software / SaaS / platforms (subscription, high incremental margin)
NOW.weight: Growth + retention + FCF conversion + rule-of-40 style quality.

lines.why: SaaS value is durable growth and expansion.
lines.good_looks_like: Solid growth; net retention >100% if disclosed; guide intact.
lines.red_flag: Growth cliff, guide cut, or AI-at-risk seat compression.

lines.why: Mature software should convert earnings to cash.
lines.good_looks_like: Positive/rising FCF margins; gross margin stable/high.
lines.red_flag: FCF negative without hyper growth; gross margin collapse.

lines.why: SBC can fake profitability.
lines.good_looks_like: SBC as % revenue contained; buybacks offset dilution.
lines.red_flag: Huge SBC with no FCF; endless dilution.

lines.why: Growth + FCF margin is the quality screen.
lines.good_looks_like: Growth% + FCF margin% competitive for the subsector.
lines.red_flag: Neither growth nor FCF working.

lines.why: Multiple compression follows estimate cuts.
lines.good_looks_like: Revisions up or stable.
lines.red_flag: Persistent downward revisions at a rich multiple.

NOW.note: Answer each line briefly before a BUY. Model-specific: do not force SaaS FCF rules on capex-growth names, or ignore FCF on mature compounders.

HPE.label: Capex-growth / AI capacity scale-up (neocloud, infra buildout)
HPE.weight: Revenue growth, estimate *direction*, liquidity, utilization narrative — NOT near-term FCF vs SaaS peers.

lines.why: Scale-ups are judged on whether demand is real and accelerating.
lines.good_looks_like: High / sustained revenue growth; fwd growth still elevated; revisions stable or up.
lines.red_flag: Growth decelerating hard while the multiple still prices perfection; large negative EPS revisions.

lines.why: Negative FCF is normal only if the balance sheet can fund the build.
lines.good_looks_like: Large cash, manageable net debt, access to capital, current ratio healthy.
lines.red_flag: Cash burn path that exhausts runway without clear funding; covenant / refinance stress.

lines.why: FCF will look 'bad' during build — ask if capex is productive capacity.
lines.good_looks_like: Capex tied to capacity customers will rent; management frames path to utilization.
lines.red_flag: Capex without demand visibility; FCF worsening while growth also stalls.

lines.why: Hyperscalers and custom silicon can reprice the entire model.
lines.good_looks_like: Sticky customers, differentiated capacity, pricing not in free-fall.
lines.red_flag: Price wars, TPU/ASIC displacement narrative with no rebuttal.

lines.why: Street estimates are the near-term scoreboard for a 3–90d swing.
lines.good_looks_like: EPS/revenue revisions flat to up over 30d.
lines.red_flag: Sharp downward revisions into a rich multiple.

HPE.note: Answer each line briefly before a BUY. Model-specific: do not force SaaS FCF rules on capex-growth names, or ignore FCF on mature compounders.

MU.label: Semiconductor / hardware cyclical (memory, foundry-sensitive, equipment)
MU.weight: Cycle position and inventory > headline P/E. Low fwd multiples at peak earnings are often traps.

lines.why: Earnings are mean-reverting; multiples look cheapest at the top.
lines.good_looks_like: Early/mid cycle: rising estimates, improving inventory, demand visibility (e.g. HBM).
lines.red_flag: Record margins/EPS with falling revisions — classic late cycle.

lines.why: Inventory build is the tell for semis.
lines.good_looks_like: Inventory stable or declining vs sales; supply discipline.
lines.red_flag: Inventory_building flag / channel fill while prices weaken.

lines.why: Cheap fwd P/E on peak EPS is not value.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs mid-cycle earnings power, not peak.
lines.red_flag: Thesis is only 'cheapest in group' without cycle underwriting.

lines.why: GPU/hyperscaler buyers dominate some nodes.
lines.good_looks_like: Diversified end demand or multi-year capacity contracts.
lines.red_flag: One customer can cancel the cycle.

lines.why: Revisions lead the cycle more than price alone.
lines.good_looks_like: Revisions up or stabilizing after a washout.
lines.red_flag: Revisions still rolling over into a bounce.

MU.note: Answer each line briefly before a BUY. Model-specific: do not force SaaS FCF rules on capex-growth names, or ignore FCF on mature compounders.

lines.good_looks_like: Consistent positive FCF; FCF margin healthy.

lines.why: Need growth to support the multiple.
lines.good_looks_like: Steady mid-to-high single digit or better with stability.

lines.why: Net debt / leverage must be sane.

lines.red_flag: Leverage spike without earnings power.

lines.why: Moat shows up in margins.
lines.good_looks_like: Stable/expanding.
lines.red_flag: Structural margin decay.

lines.why: Quality is not always cheap.
lines.good_looks_like: Multiple reasonable vs growth and history.
lines.red_flag: Top-decile multiple with slowing growth.

lines.why: Revisions drive near-term swings.
lines.good_looks_like: Flat to up.
lines.red_flag: Cuts into elevated expectations.
